- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70 after peak), model overreacts — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates — increase forecast slightly to avoid “too-low” bias.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early periods — if sentiment flips from negative to positive, adjust forecast to reflect new momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — add 2–3% upward adjustment if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ days.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3 days, assume model is lagging — apply early correction with 1–2% upward bias to catch momentum.
